curriculum.lesson_evidence: A safety network is a group of trusted people who can help when you feel unsafe or worried. Choose people you can reach in different places and at different times, such as family members, a teacher, a school counsellor or a neighbour, and write them on the fingers of one hand. If an adult does not listen, tell another until someone helps. Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) offers free, private counselling for young people, and in an emergency call 000.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
You feel unsafe at a friend's house and want to go home. Who could you contact and how?

FEEDBACK
Ask to use the phone, or message a safe adult such as a parent, and say, 'I want to come home.' If it is an emergency, call 000. Having a plan for different places means there is always a way to get help.

WATCH FOR
Thinking you must only tell one person. If one adult does not help, keep telling until someone does.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw your safety hand with five trusted people or services and write where and when you could contact each. Practise saying 'I feel unsafe, can you help me?' to a family member. Include 000 and Kids Helpline.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.explain:
A safety network is a group of trusted people who can help when you feel unsafe or worried. Choose people you can reach in different places and at different times, such as family members, a teacher, a school counsellor or a neighbour, and write them on the fingers of one hand. If an adult does not listen, tell another until someone helps. Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) offers free, private counselling for young people, and in an emergency call 000.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
